questions: What is the exact format-dependent code in the CLI and how should it change for HTML reports?
Should an HTML parsing library be added or can regex suffice for heading extraction?

answers.answer: The only format-dependent code is in show.ts line 46: the regex /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/ matches Markdown headings. For HTML reports, this needs to match <h[1-6] id="...">...</h[1-6]> tags instead. The slugify function and all comment commands are format-agnostic.
evidence: src/library/show.ts line 49: slugify() generates anchor from heading text
src/library/comments-list.ts: format-agnostic, works on anchor strings
src/library/comments-post.ts: format-agnostic, works on anchor strings

answers.answer: Simple regex should suffice. The CLI only needs to extract heading level (1-6), heading text, and optionally the id attribute from HTML heading tags. A regex like /<h([1-6])(?:\s+id="([^"]*)")?>(.+?)<\/h\1>/gi would work without adding a runtime dependency. The CLI currently has zero runtime dependencies and adding an HTML parser for one regex replacement would be over-engineering.
evidence: package.json: zero runtime dependencies (devDependencies only: typescript, @types/node)
show.ts: only extracts heading level and text, no complex DOM operations needed

statement: CLI impact is minimal: only the heading regex in show.ts needs updating to match HTML heading tags instead of Markdown headings. Both formats should be supported for backward compatibility with existing Markdown reports. A simple regex suffices; no new dependencies needed.
